authorization: owner, 2026-10-09: 'create the thumbnail and title options'

rules: Built from the episode's own cold-open cast and set, not invented people or working-model sketches.
Presenter in frame at about one third, on the right, serious rather than smiling; the story plays behind him.
Thumbnail text speaks to the viewer's aspiration in this episode's own terms: the verb of the one-person business. EP007 was HELP HER SELL.
Title promises the viewer will learn to run the business. Not a problem frame.
Mock feed against real comps at desktop, phone and sidebar, plus a shrink test at 168 and 320 px on white and #0f0f0f, before any pick.

cold_open.verbatim_opening: An innkeeper with twenty rooms is closing out a reservation. Good guest. Three nights, tipped housekeeping, asked about the trail behind the property. The kind of person she'd like to see again. So she goes to send a thank you note. And the email on the reservation isn't his.
cold_open.cast: The innkeeper, a woman in an olive cardigan over a cream top, dark hair in a low bun, behind a wooden front desk. The departing guest, a man with a backpack and dark jacket.
cold_open.set: A small country inn front desk: laptop, brass call bell, a glass of yellow daffodils, an open ledger, mail pigeonholes behind, windows onto woods.
cold_open.object: The reservation card showing the relay address k7m2q9x4@guest.booking.com.

titles.text: The One-Person Business That Gets Small Hotels Booking Direct
titles.note: Closest to EP007's accepted shape: names the business and what it does for the client. The verb 'gets ... booking direct' is the service's function, not an outcome promise.

titles.text: The One-Person Business Behind a Hotel's Direct Bookings
titles.note: Shorter, more curiosity than instruction. Reads well truncated on mobile, which cuts around 50 characters.

titles.text: How to Run the One-Person Business That Wins a Hotel's Guests Back
titles.note: Most explicitly a how-to, which is the instruction in the standard. Longest, and 'wins back' is close to EP006's retired WIN THEM BACK.

thumbnail_text.note: The literal verb of the service. Four words is one more than HELP HER SELL and will set smaller.
Three words, same metre as HELP HER SELL. 'Keep' is the innkeeper's aspiration, the returning guest she already knows.
Names the mechanism the episode and Short 03 both turn on. Drops the HELP HER pattern, so it reads as a different family.

recommendation.title: T1
recommendation.why: T1 matches the shape the owner already picked once and keeps the promise on the service's function rather than an outcome. X2 holds the HELP HER metre so the lockup sets at the same weight as EP007's, and 'keep them' is the innkeeper's aspiration in the cold open: the guest she would like to see again. X1 is more literal but sets smaller; X3 is the strongest line on its own and the weakest as a series.

claim_boundaries: 'Help' and 'gets ... booking direct' keep the promise on the practice's function. No claim that the service recovers a given share, saves a given amount, or that any property pays.
No figure on the thumbnail or in the title. No income framing.

Every person in the frame is AI-generated: the innkeeper and guest are the episode's own synthetic footage, the presenter is the avatar. Covered by the upload's altered-or-synthetic-content disclosure, which is a human step at upload.

plan.generator: Higgsfield gpt_image_2_5, the same route EP007 used
plan.rounds: three compositions, one per thumbnail text, then a mock feed and shrink test
plan.cap: under 10 credits for exploration, matching EP007's 7.25
plan.not_included: no 4K upscale until a pick is made; that was a separate 2-credit job on EP007

shrink_test_reading: At 168px, which is the sidebar and small-mobile size, X2 is the only one that still reads as three distinct words. X1 sets four lines so each is smaller and 'BOOK THEM DIRECT' closes up. X3's two long words fill the line box and the third line drops away. This is a legibility observation from the rendered test, not a preference.
what_is_not_done: No 4K upscale. EP007 upscaled only after the pick; that was a separate 2-credit job.
No owner pick. These are options.
No upload, no thumbnail set in YouTube Studio, no launch/links.json entry.

framing_round_2.prompted_by: owner, 2026-10-09: 'no i dont want the same exact framing for this. let's change it'
framing_round_2.reading: Round 1 reproduced EP007's composition exactly: presenter in the right third, thumb pointing back, three lines of type down the left. The owner is rejecting that layout for this episode, not the standard behind it. What stays: the episode's own cold-open cast and set, the presenter in frame for authenticity, text that speaks to the viewer's aspiration in this episode's terms, and the claim boundaries. What changes: where everyone sits in the frame.
framing_round_2.experiment_design: All four carry the same words, HELP HER KEEP THEM, so framing is the only variable. Choosing a frame and choosing a line are separate decisions and mixing them would make neither readable.

framings.name: Beside her, behind the desk
framings.what: The presenter is inside the scene, standing beside the innkeeper on the staff side of the counter, both over her laptop, he turns to camera. Reads as working alongside her rather than presenting at the viewer.

framings.name: Across the desk, two-shot
framings.what: Camera down the length of the counter. The innkeeper on her side, the presenter on the guest side, the open guest book between them. A consultation, not a piece to camera.

framings.name: Object forward
framings.what: The laptop screen and the reservation fill the foreground with the relay address on it, innkeeper soft behind, presenter small at the right edge. The mechanism is the hook and the people are context.

framings.name: Wide room
framings.what: The inn's front hall wide and quiet, innkeeper small behind her desk, presenter standing nearer camera at left but not dominating. Cinematic rather than a face in the corner.

unchanged: that no pick has been made

readings.F1: Warm and equal, and the only one where both faces are large. But he is standing behind the counter on the staff side, which reads as a second innkeeper or a partner in the business. That is the claim boundary this episode has to hold: the practice helps the inn, it does not run it. A caption cannot undo what the picture says. Flagged, not fatal, but it is the one with a boundary problem.
readings.F2: The relationship is right: he is on the guest side, she is behind the counter, and the open guest book between them is the episode's own mechanism. Reads as a working conversation she is part of rather than a piece to camera. Survives 168px with both people still recognisable.
readings.F3: Strongest text at every size and the relay address is the episode's actual hook. Two costs: the screen is unreadable below about 320px, so the hook only works large; and his face is cropped hard at the right edge, which looks like an accident rather than a choice.
readings.F4: The best photograph of the four and the most unlike anything else in the lane. At 168px she disappears into the background and it becomes a man alone in a room, which loses the 'her' the line depends on.

framing_round_2.shrink_test_reading: At 168px F2 and F3 hold. F1's single line across the top goes thin and both figures shrink. F4 loses the innkeeper entirely. This is read off the rendered test.

recommendation.why: It is the only one that is both legible at 168px and correct about who is who. F3 is the stronger image at full size but its hook dies small and the edge crop reads as a mistake. F1 is the warmest and has the boundary problem. F4 is the best photograph and the weakest thumbnail.
